objectives.text: Keep Azali Assoumani's personal rule intact after the disputed January 2024 vote. The electoral commission first announced 63% for him (16 January 2024); the Supreme Court confirmed 57.2% (24 January); the opposition's annulment demand and the protests were answered with a curfew from 18 January and at least one death.

objectives.text: Keep the claim to Mayotte on the record. Comoros put the claim before the UN General Assembly in its 2012 general-debate statement, and France's 1976 Security Council veto of a draft recognising Comorian sovereignty (11 votes in favour) has blocked the one UN route to it ever since.

constraints.text: Post-electoral fragility. The January 2024 protests left at least one dead and at least 25 injured, a curfew ran from 18 January, and internet access was disrupted (Reuters and AP reports, as cited by Wikipedia; not opened). A regime that has to hold its own result has less room in the external arena where the Mayotte claim is argued.

paradoxes.text: Beijing congratulated Azali on his re-election on 29 January 2024, in the same month the US embassy asked the authorities for full transparency and clarification of the results. The claim to Mayotte gains its audience in New York, where France's 1976 veto has blocked it, and loses credibility on the ballot that the government had to defend with a curfew.

grand_strategy.reading: Comoros is a small state whose founding claim to Mayotte is its main diplomatic asset, pursued at the UN because a 1976 French veto closed the Security Council to it. Under Azali the regime's international standing rests on a patron that does not ask about elections (Beijing congratulated him in January 2024, while the US embassy asked for clarification) and on a presidency that the 2024 vote and the curfew left more personal, not less. The succession to his son, the Gulf and Indian Ocean ties and the French flows the brief lists are not covered by the sources read in this pass, so they stay open.

stances.note: Claimed, not controlled: France has administered Mayotte throughout, and Comoros claims the island in its own UN statements (2012 general debate). The UN record of the claim is the 1976 Security Council veto by France of a draft recognising Comorian sovereignty, which had 11 votes in favour. Bond grievance: an open wound from independence that the Comorian state has never closed. Trend stable: no source read shows the claim softening. Confidence B: two tier 1 UN records, cited through Wikipedia and not opened here; the date of the claim as a whole (independence, 1975) is not cited and the since field uses the first UN record.

stances.note: Rival, not partner: the claim sets Comoros against the state that administers Mayotte, and France's 1976 Security Council veto is the friction on record. Confidence C: no source read uses the word rival; the grade is our reading of competing claims, and the stance is marked as such. Comoros also has a security tie with Paris (a 1978 security treaty, and French troops after the 1989 coup, both cited through Wikipedia to a Library of Congress country study that was not opened). A reading of reluctant ally would take that tie as alignment; no source read calls it reluctant, so the grade stays rival until the next pass checks the treaty's status. Bond grievance: Mayotte.

stances_toward.note: Paris runs a partnership with Moroni: the joint press conference of Macron and Azali Assoumani on 22 July 2019 set out the aim of a strategic partnership, and the French Treasury describes France as a major economic partner (2024 trade of about EUR 42.9m). Partner, not ally: no defence treaty is read here, and the security tie that the Comorian record dates to 1978 was not checked. Paris does not ignore Mayotte: Macron called it a territorial dispute ("contentieux") of more than 44 years in 2019, so the claim is named and set aside, not dropped. Bond grievance: the Mayotte question is an open wound between the two states, as the Comoros card reads it, and the 1976 veto stays on the record. Stable is our reading; the sources read do not cover 2025-26 clearly. Confidence B: two French official sources (the 2019 Elysee statement and the Treasury page), read through search summaries and not opened in full.
